title: A tri-phase fuel electrode enabling low-temperature co-firing of high-performance reversible protonic ceramic cells
content: Reversible protonic ceramic cells (RPCCs) offer significant potential for efficient energy conversion and storage at intermediate temperatures. However, their widespread deployment is limited by the high sintering temperatures needed for electrolyte densification, which can cause Ba volatilization and cell bending, compromising structural integrity, and manufacturing reliability – as well by the electrochemical limitations of conventional Ni-BaZr0.1Ce0.7Y0.1Yb0.1O3−δ (BZCYYb) (6 : 4 wt%) bi-phase cermet fuel electrodes. Here, we report a fundamental departure from the long-dominant bi-phase cermet paradigm by introducing BaCo0.4Fe0.4Zr0.1Y0.1O3−δ (BCFZY) as a third functional phase in the Ni-BZCYYb fuel electrode support layer, resulting in a novel Ni-BZCYYb-BCFZY (6 : 3 : 1 wt%) tri-phase composite fuel electrode. The incorporation of BCFZY, as a multifunctional BZCYYb-substituting phase with superior sinterability compared to BZCYYb, allows for full electrolyte densification at sintering temperatures as low as 1200–1300 °C. This represents a reduction of 150–250 °C compared to conventional methods, achieved without the use of sintering aids in the electrolyte layer. The lowered co-sintering temperature effectively suppresses grain coarsening in all constituent phases, preserving a fine-particle microstructure with enhanced open porosity that is crucial for electrochemical activity. Under reducing fuel electrode conditions, BCFZY undergoes spontaneous in situ Co exsolution, generating uniformly distributed metallic Co nanoparticles. These nanoparticles simultaneously enhance electronic conductivity and catalytic activity for hydrogen oxidation and evolution, functioning as a self-activating multifunctional phase. The 1250 °C sintered tri-phase fuel electrode-supported cells achieve a peak power density of 1.14 W cm−2 in fuel cell mode and a current density of 1.47 A cm−2 at 1.3 V in electrolysis mode at 550 °C. This demonstrates a substantial performance enhancement over conventional Ni-BZCYYb cells, particularly at operating temperatures below 550 °C. Notably, stable operation has been achieved in protonic ceramic cells, with 4 A cm−2 in fuel cell mode and 5 A cm−2 in electrolysis mode. Long-term stability evaluations conducted over 690 hours, which included high-current reversible cycling, thermal cycling, and fuel starvation, confirm robust durability of the cell. These findings establish the Ni-BZCYYb-BCFZY tri-phase architecture as a new paradigm for fuel electrode design, redefining the performance and manufacturability boundaries of RPCCs.
